subject: Re: Availability guarantee — baseline and rollback language
messages:
From: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@falconfintech.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@falconfintech.com>
Date: 2025-07-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Availability baseline + requested exception for batch workloads

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput looked great. Before procurement gets to signatures, ops has a couple of asks on the SLA template:

- For the first 6 months of the pilot we want an operational carve-out for nightly batch inference jobs (these are large KV cache warm-ups that bump tail latency). Practically, wed like the baseline uptime to be 99.9% instead of 99.95% for month 1-6, with full 99.95% reverting after that period.
- If we accept the temporary baseline, wed expect the monthly credit calculation to be the standard per-minute remedy, but capped at a single monthly pool (max one monthly credit payout per invoice month) rather than multiple incident payouts.

Attached is a short matrix of our workload windows. Can Redwood confirm if youll accept the 6-month baseline rollback and the single monthly remedy pool?

Stuart
Head of Ops, Falcon Fintech
Attachments: Falcon_SLA_Redline_v2.pdf, operational-matrix.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@falconfintech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability baseline + requested exception for batch workloads

Hi Stuart — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the matrix. Ive looped in Ben (sales) and Laura (legal) so we can run through the operational and contract-side implications.

Quick reply on feasibility: we can consider a temporary baseline at 99.9% for a defined pilot window, but well need:
- precise start/end dates tied to the signed SOW;
- a telemetry definition (what counts as an incident vs scheduled batch window) — Redwood will provide a draft ops definition;
- clarity on how credits are calculated if an incident originates inside a scheduled batch window but impacts serving outside of it.

Ben / Laura / Markus (ops reviewer) — could you weigh in on the monthly pool cap and whether the rollback clause can be time-boxed and automatic (i.e., reverts after X days unless Falcon provides written notice)?

Thanks,
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@falconfintech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-05T12:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability baseline + requested exception for batch workloads

Stuart — appreciate the detail, this is a reasonable operational ask for a pilot. A couple of commercial points from our side:

1) Monthly remedy pool: Redwood is open to a single monthly payout (one remedy computed against the aggregate downtime metric) for the pilot, provided the maximum payout does not exceed 10% of the monthly invoice for the pilot months. That cap protects us from disproportionate single-incident impacts.

2) Rollback / automatic reversion: we can accept automatic reversion to standard uptime (99.95%) after a fixed 180-day pilot, unless Falcon requests an extension in writing 30 days before expiry.

3) Incident attribution: if a scheduled batch causes an out-of-window failure, our ops team will use the request traces and KV cache timelines to attribute the root cause. Where attribution is ambiguous, we propose an independent triage within 5 business days with both parties.

Markus — can your team draft the "telemetry definition" lauren mentioned (simple list: measurement source, observation window, what is a scheduled batch event)?

Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@falconfintech.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@falconfintech.com>
Date: 2025-07-06T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability baseline + requested exception for batch workloads

Thanks — quick clarifications from our engineering side:

- The batch windows are nightly 01:00-04:00 PT and a weekly full-refresh Sunday 02:00-06:00 PT. Wed expect those times to be treated as scheduled windows in the telemetry definition.
- On the remedy cap: 10% of the invoice for the pilot months is acceptable if the definition of "invoice" excludes any one-time onboarding fees.

Also — procurement asked whether the monthly pool approach will preserve the same customer-facing SLA language that appears in public docs (we prefer minimal consumer-facing change; internal SOW can capture the pilot exception).

Maya
Engineering Lead, Falcon Fintech

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@falconfintech.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-07T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability baseline + requested exception for batch workloads — contract redline notes

Folks — I reviewed Falcons redline and Bens commercial suggestion. A couple of contract points to capture clearly:

- Pilot exception clause: define pilot period start (SOW effective date) and fixed 180-day duration; include explicit acceptance criteria for rollback (automatic unless written extension).
- Monthly remedy pool: include formula and cap language. Proposed clause language: "For the pilot period only, the parties agree a single monthly remedy shall be calculated based on aggregate unavailability minutes during a calendar month, with a maximum payout equal to ten percent (10%) of Redwood's recurring charges for such month, excluding one-time onboarding or professional services fees."
- Maintenance carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows should be expressly excluded. If Falcon requires scheduled batch windows to be treated similarly, we need them listed in the SOW Appendix A and timeboxed.
- Telemetry and dispute resolution: include a 5-business-day joint triage step and an escalation path to a neutral technical reviewer if unresolved after 10 business days.

Ive attached a contract snippet for internal review. Once we align internally, we can circulate a tracked-redline to Falcon.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Falcon_SLA_Redline_v2.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@falconfintech.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@falconfintech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-08T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability baseline + requested exception for batch workloads — next steps

Stuart / Maya — thanks for the quick turn. Summary / next steps from Redwood: 

1) We will produce a short telemetry definition draft (Markus) and a clean contract snippet (Laura) by Tue 2025-07-10.
2) Redwood agrees in-principle to a 180-day pilot with automatic reversion to 99.95% unless Falcon requests an extension 30 days prior to expiry.
3) Commercial cap: monthly remedy pool capped at 10% of recurring monthly invoice for pilot months; onboarding fees excluded.
4) Operational requirement: Falcon will add the nightly and weekly batch windows to SOW Appendix A so they are expressly recognized as scheduled windows.

Ill circulate an internal consolidated redline and then a tracked version to you both. If this sounds right, can you confirm and well lock dates and get procurement and legal to exchange documents?

Thanks,
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
